_source: Microsoft ElectionGuard reference implementation (github.com/microsoft/electionguard-python), published sample data: data/plaintext_ballots_simple.json (6 ballots) tallied against data/election_manifest_simple.json. Fetched 2026-07-14 from raw.githubusercontent.com/microsoft/electionguard-python/main/. Selection order and votes_allowed are taken verbatim from the manifest's ballot_selections sequence_order.
_framing: INTEROP SANITY CHECK, NOT CONFORMANCE. ElectionGuard uses integer ElGamal modulo a large prime p; Saksi uses ristretto255 elliptic-curve ElGamal. Ciphertext bytes, nonces, and proof systems therefore differ and are NOT comparable. What is pinned here is the plaintext tally SEMANTICS both exponential-ElGamal voting schemes must agree on: encrypt each per-selection {0,1} choice, homomorphically add the ciphertexts, threshold/secret decrypt, and recover the SAME per-selection totals ElectionGuard's own published ballots produce. These are REAL ElectionGuard sample ballots (not authored toy data): multi-select contests (votes_allowed>1) and undervotes appear, so the invariant is per-ballot selected-count <= votes_allowed, NOT exactly-one.
